item.title: Americans don’t have to choose between our AI future and ripping off copyright owners
item.description: The DOJ's embrace of fair use for AI training breaks with the White House's own framework, as OpenAI, Microsoft and news groups battle over copyright.
item.content:encoded:
One of the biggest court battles over artificial intelligence (AI) is putting an age-old legal principle to the test — and raising important questions about the Trump administration's AI policy.

Several news organizations, including The New York Times, are suing OpenAI and Microsoft for using millions of newspaper articles to train AI systems. The newspapers argue that the tech firms violated basic copyright protections. The tech firms contend that training their models on those articles qualifies as "fair use," a longstanding principle that allows copyrighted material to be used in certain ways without permission from or compensation to the copyright owner.

The Department of Justice (DOJ) has sided squarely with OpenAI's position — breaking with the administration's previously more balanced stance on the issue. The DOJ filed a statement of interest embracing an extreme vision of fair use that would grant AI companies virtually unfettered access to copyrighted material for commercial training, without obtaining permission from or compensating the creators whose works fuel these systems.

MIKE DAVIS: THE TRUMP DOJ SHOULD WITHDRAW ITS STATEMENT OF INTEREST IN THE OPENAI LAWSUIT

This expansive interpretation threatens to turn a narrow copyright exception into a blanket exemption for the world's most powerful and profitable industries.

The DOJ's reasoning is that requiring a copyright license for material used in AI training would impose high costs on AI developers. It claims those costs could make it harder for small companies to compete and hamper U.S. AI leadership and national security.

FOX NEWS POLL: VOTERS SEE AI REGULATION AS URGENT, RANK SAFEGUARDS AHEAD OF INNOVATION

Those concerns deserve consideration. But the DOJ's aggressive arguments in the brief depart from more measured guidance elsewhere in the administration. The White House's official AI framework acknowledges valid arguments on both sides of the copyright debate.

Likewise, the Carolina Principles for Emerging Technologies, adopted by G20 ministers at the Commerce Department's recent Innovation Ministerial, recognize that the intersection of AI and copyright poses "complex legal and policy questions." The principles note the "essential role" of copyright protections in supporting creators and call for respecting IP as a pillar of G20 AI policy.

MUSIC INDUSTRY FENDS OFF FLOOD OF AI MUSIC 'STEALING' THE CHARTS

The DOJ statement also overlooks how its stance could favor larger AI companies over smaller firms and startups. Several AI startups have argued that paying for the material they use provides more reliable access to training material, reduces legal uncertainty and improves models. Other companies have emerged to aggregate copyrights and make licensing easier.

It's particularly problematic for large AI companies to complain about paying for access to copyrighted materials. They are among the best positioned to pay for those materials, and doing so would help develop the kind of licensing markets they claim are lacking.

OBAMA CRITICIZES TRUMP ON APPROACH TO AI, ESCALATES WARNING FOR STRONGER REGULATION

And even if national security were a legitimate justification, the government could not simply disregard property rights. The Constitution and other laws require just compensation when private property is taken for public use, and intellectual property rights are still property rights. Letting AI firms appropriate creators' IP without permission or compensation would be akin to letting data center builders seize private land without paying fair value.

If courts adopt the DOJ's position that fair use protects AI developers in virtually all circumstances, it would reduce incentives to create new works. Copyrights encourage creative work by assuring writers, artists and other creators that their work can't be easily stolen or copied. Licensing those rights allows creators to earn a living and underpins over $1 trillion in U.S. economic activity.

Weaker copyrights could result in fewer human-created books, articles, research papers, films and songs. Ironically, that could eventually leave AI systems with fewer and lower-quality materials to train on – a scenario that serves no one's interests.

All of this is why the Trump administration would be wise to follow its own AI framework and let the court system evaluate AI copyright disputes case by case, rather than arguing for unfettered fair use exceptions.

Policymakers also have a role to play. One promising bill is the bipartisan CLEAR Act. Introduced in February by California Democrat Sen. Adam Schiff and Utah Republican Sen. John Curtis, the CLEAR Act would require AI developers to publicly disclose the copyrighted works used in each new generative-AI model's training dataset.

The proposal would not settle whether any particular training practice qualifies as fair use. But it would give creators more information about whether their work helped train an AI system, enabling them to pursue appropriate compensation or other remedies when they believe their rights have been violated.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE FOX NEWS OPINION

That kind of targeted reform offers a useful model for copyright enforcement in the age of AI. Rather than treating licensing as an obstacle to innovation, policymakers should foster a market where AI developers can efficiently license copyrighted material while respecting creators' rights.

AI innovation is vital to America's future. But America's creative industries still depend on strong copyright protections. Policymakers need to promote both.

item.title: Cardinals may start their fourth QB in four weeks as Carson Beck has injury after first career start
item.description: Carson Beck's back spasms could push the Arizona Cardinals to 40-year-old Josh Johnson, their fourth starting quarterback in four weeks, versus the Chiefs.
item.content:encoded:
The Arizona Cardinals quarterback carousel is still spinning.

After just one start, Cardinals rookie Carson Beck is dealing with back spasms and may not play Sunday against the Kansas City Chiefs. If the 25-year-old cannot play, the Cardinals will turn to 40-year-old Josh Johnson.

If Johnson starts, it will be the Cardinals' fourth different starting quarterback in four weeks. Head coach Mike LaFleur reported Friday that they will see how Beck responds to treatment tomorrow, and that he doesn't think Beck will be out multiple weeks.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE

"You go with the people who know what they’re doing to treat it. It’s not like this is the first time he’s dealt with it," LaFleur said. "We’ll see more tomorrow."

Beck had dealt with back spasms earlier in the season. The former Miami star quarterback went 11 for 18 for 108 yards with two interceptions in the Cardinals' 34-6 loss to the Los Angeles Rams in his first career start Sunday.

For LaFleur, he has familiarity with Johnson, as he was the offensive coordinator with the New York Jets in 2021 and called plays for the journeyman quarterback then.

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

"Cool part is, if it is Josh, I’ve called plays for him before and had a really great experience calling plays for him," LaFleur said. "So, we’ll go shoot our shot and I expect nothing less from our guys."

If you told Cardinals fans a month ago that the team might be on its fourth different starting quarterback in four weeks, they'd be pretty surprised. In Week 8, the Cardinals started Jacoby Brissett against the Dallas Cowboys. He was benched in the second half for Gardner Minshew II, and the former Jacksonville Jaguars starter led the team to a thrilling comeback.

In the aftermath of that, the Cardinals named Minshew the starting quarterback and traded Brissett to the Baltimore Ravens. In Week 9, Minshew's first start, he suffered a UCL injury that required season-ending surgery.

With Brissett in Baltimore and Minshew hurt, the Cardinals started Beck in Week 10 and now might be turning to Johnson in Week 11. Adding to the chaos, Johnson only joined the Cardinals on Nov. 10, when the team signed him off the Cincinnati Bengals practice squad.

The 3-7 Cardinals play the 7-2 Chiefs on Sunday at 1:00 p.m. ET.

item.title: Knicks star Jalen Brunson reveals how he really feels about 'King of New York' nickname
item.description: Jalen Brunson reacted to "King of New York" talk after leading the New York Knicks to their first NBA title in 53 years during a recent interview.
item.content:encoded:
When you help lead the New York Knicks to its first NBA title in 53 years, in a city that hasn’t seen a "Big Four" team win their championship since the New York Giants in 2011, you get called the "King of New York."

After all, ask anyone around the five boroughs and they’ll tell you: New York City is a basketball town when the Knicks are on top.

Jalen Brunson, the NBA Finals MVP and Knicks superstar point guard, has been hearing "King of New York" thrown around from friends and fans alike since the victory over the San Antonio Spurs this past summer. It’s a moniker synonymous with greatness in a city that begs for it with all its teams and superstar athletes.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE

To hear it means you’ve accomplished greatness in a city that demands it each season, or else the year is a failure. There’s pressure enough to play in the "World’s Greatest Arena" in Madison Square Garden as the face of the Knicks, but how does Brunson handle being called "King of New York?"

His answer tells you exactly where his mindset is this season, and the many to come.

"To be honest with you, I don’t want to say it’s annoying. It’s more of like when people say that, it’s cool to hear," he told OutKick in a recent interview, while highlighting his partnership with Lowe’s ahead of their big Black Friday activation. "A lot of people who I know, know I don’t like it. So, they’ll just say it to annoy me."

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

Brunson doesn’t have to explain why he doesn’t like it. The Villanova product has always gone about his business, staying humble and never being boisterous, though he has every reason to be considering what he’s accomplished alongside his Knicks teammates.

Yes, he’s won a championship, perhaps the one title that meant more than the rest in this great city. But his answer says many things, including one isn’t enough.

However, to be called "King of New York" — the same nickname Babe Ruth, Mickey Mantle, Lawrence Taylor, Mark Messier, Eli Manning, Derek Jeter and many others have worn over the years — is something Brunson appreciates.

Even if he doesn’t feel that way himself.

"The one thing that I’ll always think about is when you’re working to achieve something, like a goal to win a championship, you’d be surprised of all the little things that come with it," he explained. "The things that are cool, the things that are not. The pros and cons to it.'

"So, just to be thrown in that conversation with a lot of New York athlete greats, I mean, it’s a real honor. It’s something I don’t take lightly. I would never proclaim myself that."

KNICKS STAR JALEN BRUNSON IS A MAN OF THE PEOPLE, REVEALS THE ONE THING HE CAN'T LIVE WITHOUT

He may not call himself "King of New York," but that’s not going to stop the scores of Knicks fans who can’t help themselves if they see him outside The Garden.

He’s earned it, but in Brunson’s mind, there’s more to be accomplished, including defending that title this season.

Brunson will be in the midst of his back-to-back title pursuit with the Knicks on Black Friday, but as Lowe’s "Bucket Expert," he’s also spreading the word about the company’s exciting deals including a customer-favorite "Black Friday Mystery Bucket."

On Nov. 27, the first 150 MyLowe’s Rewards members at participating Lowe’s stores will receive exclusive giveaways, and additionally, more than $15 million in prizes will be available for four lucky MyLowe’s Rewards members at every store.

The first 50 members at each store will receive a free Lowe’s Black Friday Mystery Bucket packed with 10-plus products and offers, and four members of the first 50 will win one of the day’s top prizes: A free appliance under $2,000, an EGO Outdoor power tool, a Blackstone grilling package or a CRAFTSMANtools package.

With deals abundant, Brunson is excited to be involved.

"It’s a really cool thing to be a part of. I’m just honored to be associated with Lowe’s and this deal. Happy to be a part of it," he said.

Brunson added, "You’re doing yourself a disservice," if you intend on hitting Lowe’s on Black Friday and not signing up for MyLowe’s Rewards, as those who are not members can sign up for free ahead of Nov. 27.

item.title: Trump floats an unexpected name to be his successor as powerhouses Rubio and Vance stand by
item.description: Donald Trump stunned the White House press briefing room by asking Stephen Miller if he wants to run for president, as JD Vance and Marco Rubio looked on.
item.content:encoded:
During a lighthearted Friday afternoon moment with the media inside the White House press briefing room, President Donald Trump floated a new name to succeed him as president, while two expected 2028 hopefuls stood by.

The president asked the media if they'd like to continue with the press conference — where Trump provided updates on his trip to China where he met with Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin. This prompted laughs from Vice President JD Vance and Secretary of State Marco Rubio, who flanked him on either side during the briefing.

Then, he asked newly-minted Chief of Staff Stephen Miller, whom he called the "most powerful man in the world," to speak with members of the press.

MAGA VOTERS REVEAL WHO THEY WANT TO SEE LEAD GOP IN 2028

Miller took the podium and launched into a more than two-minute speech listing Trump's accomplishments from the first two years of his second term in office.

"I just wanted to say that what President Trump has achieved over the last two years is more than any president has achieved by far in American history. We can stand up here for four hours and go through achievement by achievement by achievement," Miller said.

He then rattled some of them off, including:

"Under his leadership, the next two years are going to be the greatest two years in American history," Miller said. "And I'm so proud to be his chief of staff to oversee on his behalf the staff in this building to keep delivering wins for this extraordinary American leader."

Trump was clearly impressed with Miller, who stepped in to replace Susie Wiles earlier this month following sweeping midterm losses for Republicans.

"We have breaking news! Breaking news!" Trump said. "He was better than these two guys," he added, turning towards Vance and Rubio, who both also spoke at the press conference.

"Do you want to run for president?" Trump asked Miller as he was leaving the podium, prompting laughter from the group.

STEPHEN MILLER'S INTERNAL MEMO UNLEASHES TRUMP AGENCIES AFTER 'ABSOLUTE CONTROL' UNDER WILES' REIGN

No major names from either party have yet to announce their intentions to run for president in 2028. But with the midterms finished, rumors have swirled about who will toss their hats in the ring.

Vance and Rubio are widely viewed as the two most viable options for Republicans.

Miller's name has not been previously floated as a contender for launching a White House bid.

item.title: LSU's $40 million football roster may have been a mirage, according to CFB expert Josh Pate
item.description: Josh Pate says LSU's $40-50 million roster under Lane Kiffin missed at quarterback, and the Tigers' 6-4 record could leave them out of the CFP race.
item.content:encoded:
It's safe to say things aren't going the way anyone had planned for the LSU Tigers' football team in 2026.

Most fans and rivals agreed that when the Bayou Bengals went out and poached Lane Kiffin from Ole Miss and paired him with a roster that was reported to be between $40-50 million, year one was already being tagged with sky-high expectations.

Fast forward to mid-November, and not only are Kiffin and the Tigers out of the running for the SEC Championship, they are projected to miss the College Football Playoff entirely thanks to their shocking 6-4 record.

LANE KIFFIN BLAMES LSU'S $40+ MILLION ROSTER AFTER LOSS TO TEXAS: 'WE'LL HAVE BETTER ROSTERS’

Even potential wins against top-ten Tennessee this weekend and Golden Boot rivals Arkansas after Thanksgiving would do little to improve LSU's standing in the CFP polls.

So, what went wrong?

They hired the best available coach, paired him with an all-star staff that included one of the best defensive coordinators in the game in Blake Baker and armed him with one of the most expensive rosters in college football.

Shouldn't that be enough to expect a home run in year one?

College football commentator Josh Pate isn't buying the idea that an expensive roster guarantees success in this day and age.

JOSH PATE WAS EVICTED WHILE EARNING $27K. NOW, HE RUNS A COLLEGE FOOTBALL MEDIA EMPIRE

"I guess he enters next year on the hot seat," Pate said sarcastically while replying to a question from one of his viewers.

"I'm not asking anyone to feel sorry for Lane Kiffin," he continued.

Pate would go on to explain that giving someone unlimited resources doesn't always equate to leveling up, and Kiffin is no different.

"People kept throwing around that same data point: $40 million roster... What it was (was) LSU going and hiring their dream candidate at head coach, and then them just recklessly throwing around as much money as they could in the portal to put together a team to compete for a national title in year one."

It sounds like a simple formula, even to those who have been paying attention to the sport for a few years now in the NIL era, but it might not be that cut and dry.

"If this same exact roster was paid $28 million, would it be different? No, it's the same roster," he points out.

Plain and simple, the Tigers might have overpaid for some of the talent on their two-deep.

"You just paid a lot of money for 'average.'"

As Pate explains, LSU's pickups in the portal were great, but they only papered over deficiencies rather than provided quality depth, and, more importantly, they missed at the most important position: quarterback.

ARCH MANNING TURNS DEATH VALLEY INTO LSU’S FUNERAL AS TEXAS BURIES LANE KIFFIN’S CFP HOPES

"They didn't whiff on this portal class, by the way," he argues. "A lot of these dudes have been studs. It's just the most important position, there's not a stud at."

To his credit, Pate has been consistent with his takes on Kiffin and LSU.

The popular YouTube host said back in July that he thought the Tigers would miss the playoff outright in year one, and that caused some consternation among the LSU faithful.

Where LSU goes from here remains a mystery, but you can rest assured that Pate's words will fall on deaf ears.

Kiffin is making too much money and has been given too many resources to fail this badly in year one.

He will be going into a pivotal year two with the expectations ratcheted up considerably.

Should he miss the CFP again in 2027, it might be time for Kiffin to start looking for a good realtor in southern Louisiana.

item.content:encoded:
Months after sparking fan concern with a frightening onstage fall, Jackson 5 icon Marlon Jackson disclosed that he has been privately battling cancer for the past four years.

"And I'm going to tell people right now, God has me," he insisted during an appearance on "The Farah Shammas Podcast." "He already told me he has me. I've had cancer for four years.

"But I'm great. I'm good," Jackson, 69, added. "Bad grass don't die. So, I'm going to be around for a long time."

Jackson explained that his road to recovery required both aggressive medical intervention and major lifestyle changes.

"I've already had my prostate gland removed, and I've had radiation treatment and everything is fine," the Jackson 5 member said. "Everything is great. I walk almost four miles, four times a week."

His lifestyle changes also included a change to his diet.

"Well, I stopped eating beef and pork in 1977 and, after the cancer, I did do away with sugar and careful what I put in my body and try to take care of myself," Jackson explained.

While adjusting his diet and exercise habits, Jackson maintained that his faith and the prayers of others have carried him through his recovery.

"I'm doing great, so I thank everybody who have prayed for me. The Lord told me, you know, cast your burdens on him, and he'll take care of them and that's what he's done, so I can't complain."

"Even my doctor said, 'You're doing so much better than what I thought.'"

Jackson took a hard fall onstage during a concert at the Wichita Riverfest on May 29.

According to fan-captured video from the performance, Jackson tripped over a piece of stage equipment while walking across the stage and singing Michael Jackson's "Wanna Be Startin' Somethin'." Despite the abrupt fall, Jackson recovered, got back up and finished the show with The Jacksons without reporting any major injuries.

Managed by their father, Joe Jackson, the original lineup consisted of five brothers: Jackie, Tito, Jermaine, Marlon and Michael Jackson. Randy Jackson joined the lineup in 1976 and the group rebranded as The Jacksons while Jermaine pursued his solo career.

During their peak, the group became the first act in recording history to have their first four major label singles reach No. 1 on the Billboard Hot 100. Their most recognizable songs include "I Want You Back," "ABC," "The Love You Save," "I'll Be There" and "Dancing Machine."

item.title: Judge rejects Alex Murdaugh's push to toss murder indictment over blood and ammo claims
item.description: A judge refused to dismiss murder charges against Alex Murdaugh, rejecting defense claims that SLED investigator David Owen misled the grand jury on blood spatter.
item.content:encoded:
The judge overseeing Alex Murdaugh’s double murder retrial has refused to dismiss the charges against him, dealing another legal blow to the disgraced former attorney ahead of his April court date.

Attorneys for Murdaugh argued on Friday, Nov. 13, during a pre-trial hearing that South Carolina Law Enforcement Division (SLED) investigator David Owen gave misleading testimony regarding blood-spatter evidence and shotgun ammunition, saying it undermined the integrity of the grand jury proceedings.

In her ruling on Friday afternoon, South Carolina Circuit Court Judge Debra R. McCaslin said that while there were major errors in the state's presentation of evidence to grand jurors, other evidence overwhelmingly supported the indictment.

"Even if the challenged testimony concerning the blood spatter on the T-shirt and shotgun ammunition were excluded from consideration by the grand jury, the remaining unchallenged evidence overwhelmingly established probable cause," McCaslin wrote.

ALEX MURDAUGH MAKES 'EXPLOSIVE' BID TO BLOW UP MURDER CASE HINGING ON DNA, DIRTY MONEY AND LIES: EXPERT

While McCaslin refused to dismiss the murder indictment, she criticized the state's lead investigator on the case.

"The Court does not take lightly Special Agent Owen’s failure to recognize and account for a laboratory report addressed directly to him prior to presenting testimony in this case," she wrote. "Oversights of this nature undermine public confidence in the integrity of the criminal justice system."

McCaslin also acknowledged that evidence regarding ammunition presented to the grand jury wasn't accurate, but says there's no evidence that it was intentional.

ALEX MURDAUGH LAWYERS ALLEGE ‘FABRICATED’ EVIDENCE WAS USED TO SECURE MURDER INDICTMENTS

READ THE ORDER HERE:

"Even accepting that the challenged testimony was inaccurate, the record presented does not establish intentional fabrication or prosecutorial misconduct," she said. 

The judge said Murdaugh's defense can challenge the disputed evidence at trial in April.

"Any inconsistencies in prior investigative statements or forensic conclusions are matters properly addressed through cross-examination and impeachment at the upcoming trial, rather than through the pretrial dismissal of facially valid indictments," McCaslin wrote.

The South Carolina Attorney General’s Office said after McCaslin's ruling: "We continue to prepare for the retrial in April."

Murdaugh's defense attorneys argued that Owen misled the grand jury about alleged blood-spatter evidence found on the shirt Murdaugh was wearing on June 7, 2021, when his wife, Maggie, and son, Paul, were murdered at the family's Moselle property in Colleton County.

Owen claimed that blood spatter found on Murdaugh's shirt linked him to the killings, despite earlier testing that failed to detect human blood in samples taken from the garment.

At Murdaugh's first murder trial, Owen said he had no intention of misleading the grand jury and stated that he did not see the final SLED lab report until after the indictment had been issued.

ALEX MURDAUGH FACES STATE PUSHBACK ON MAGGIE DNA TESTING AND PRISON LAPTOP REQUEST

Prosecutors reiterated during the Nov. 13 hearing that the negative test results regarding the blood didn't necessarily invalidate the blood-spatter findings, and pointed to additional testing done by the state's expert which suggested earlier chemical treatment could have produced false negatives.

SEND US A TIP

Prosecutors said the expert continued to stand behind his conclusions and that Owen's testimony before the grand jury accurately captured investigators' understanding of the evidence at that point in time.

ALEX MURDAUGH DEFENSE SAYS MURDER WEAPON MAY BE TIED TO SEPARATE KILLING AS JUDGE SEEKS ANSWERS

Owen also told grand jurors that shotguns found on the Murdaugh property were loaded with the same combination of ammunition used to kill Paul, a claim the defense argues was false. Murdaugh's attorneys maintained that none of the recovered shotguns contained the exact combination of shells found at the murder scene.

LISTEN TO THE NEW 'CRIME & JUSTICE WITH DONNA ROTUNNO' PODCAST

Prosecutors acknowledged that Owen's description of the ammunition to the grand jury may have been imprecise but argued that he had not intentionally misled jurors.

"This was not overtly false. This was what the agent understood at the time," lead prosecutor Creighton Waters said.

Murdaugh was convicted of both murders in 2023, but the South Carolina Supreme Court later overturned the convictions after finding that former Colleton County Clerk of Court Becky Hill improperly influenced the jury . His retrial is scheduled to begin April 5, 2027.

item.title: Tom Brady calls out NFL's increasingly elaborate touchdown celebrations: 'Learn your assignments'
item.description: Tom Brady said NFL players should learn their assignments, lamenting he's seen more choreography in touchdown celebrations than in a Broadway show.
item.content:encoded:
For Tom Brady, at some point, enough is enough.

The NFL legend was asked about the Detroit Lions' wild human centipede celebration they did in Germany, and Brady wants players to focus on their actual assignments instead of elaborate touchdown celebrations.

"Yeah, of course I couldn't miss it. Look, I played with guys that couldn't remember their third-down assignments, that blocked the wrong people in the run game, that, you know, jumped offsides when it was clearly the cadence was on one. Except when now they get into the end zone, they can remember a 12-person choreographed centipede celebration," Brady said in a clip posted to Fox Sports' X account.

"I've seen more choreography in some of these touchdown celebrations than in a Broadway show. Okay, learn your assignments. How about that?"

Touchdown celebrations started becoming more extravagant after the NFL relaxed the rules in May 2017. After that rule change, players could use the football as a prop, celebrate on the ground and stage larger group celebrations.

In that first season after the rule was relaxed, players became creative in their celebrations. The Minnesota Vikings orchestrated a game of duck-duck-goose, which was led by tight end Kyle Rudolph.

The Kansas City Chiefs mocked a potato sack race, as Travis Kelce, Tyreek Hill and DeMarcus Robinson hopped across the end zone. In 2023, the Miami Dolphins pretended to get buckled and ride a roller coaster after scoring a touchdown.

Yet for Brady, at some point, enough is enough. Less theatrics, more focus on football.

item.title: EXCLUSIVE: Trump’s former FDA nominee vowed new abortion pill safety review after pressure from Sen Hawley
item.description: Food and Drug Administration nominee Dr. Heidi Overton committed to a timeline for a delayed mifepristone safety study, Sen. Josh Hawley's office says.
item.content:encoded:
FIRST ON FOX: Dr. Heidi Overton, a former nominee for Food and Drug Administration (FDA) commissioner, had committed to establishing a binding timeline and clear parameters for a safety study on the abortion medication mifepristone, the office of Sen. Josh Hawley, R-Mo., told Fox News Digital Friday.

Hawley, a member of the Senate Health, Education, Labor and Pensions (HELP) Committee, has spent months pressing federal health officials for accountability over the delayed assessment.

"These are major pro-life wins that help ensure a robust study and the potential reinstatement of critical safeguards on the abortion drug that President Biden stripped away," Hawley said in a statement to Fox News Digital. 

"I will expect that the FDA will live up to these promises, and as a member of the HELP Committee, any future FDA commissioner nominee must commit to carrying this through in order to earn my support."

TRUMP TO NOMINATE DR HEIDI OVERTON AS NEXT FDA COMMISSIONER

The White House pulled Heidi Overton’s nomination one day before a Senate committee vote. President Donald Trump hailed Overton as a "ROCKSTAR" in August when he picked the physician and White House advisor to succeed Marty Makary, who resigned in May.

According to Hawley's office, the Trump administration had pledged to finalize a comprehensive mifepristone safety study by March 2027, with the FDA committing to enact regulatory changes supported by the findings no later than September 2027.

Updated safety protocols would have applied to both brand-name mifepristone and its generic equivalents.

FEDERAL APPEALS COURT BLOCKS MAILING OF ABORTION PILLS IN RULING WITH NATIONWIDE EFFECT

Hawley's office noted that the potential study will analyze Medicaid and commercially available data spanning periods before and after the Biden administration lifted restrictions.

Federal oversight of the medication has drawn sustained scrutiny since 2023, when the Biden administration eliminated requirements mandating in-person doctor visits and in-person dispensing.

HAWLEY URGES DOJ PROBE INTO ABORTION PILL MAKER OVER SAFETY CONCERNS

The FDA's review has faced repeated postponements despite earlier pledges by officials to release a study in 2025 amid concerns from critics that the agency was excluding critical data.

"FDA has explained its intention to quickly complete its ongoing review using appropriate data and qualified experts, follow the evidence, and make the scientific basis and results public to the greatest extent permitted by law," Overton wrote in her Senate committee confirmation questionnaire prior to her nomination being pulled.

WHITE HOUSE PULLS TRUMP’S FDA PICK HEIDI OVERTON ON EVE OF SENATE PANEL VOTE

"If confirmed, I would support completing that work as expeditiously as practicable while preserving the integrity of the scientific review," she added.

In March, Hawley urged fellow Republicans to back his legislation to ban mifepristone.

"The evidence is now clear," he said at the time. "Mifepristone is almost always fatal to the unborn child, but it is also significantly dangerous for women. The drug companies that make this drug know this but continue to profit from the drug’s nearly unregulated distribution, largely insulated from liability. Congress can no longer ignore these dangers."

item.title: Iran takes pointed jab at Trump Cabinet secretary for moving onto military base
item.description: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent moved to a military base amid reported Iranian assassination threats a senior official says reached an advanced stage.
item.content:encoded:
Iran mocked Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent, calling the official "sweetie" on social media after reports emerged that he had moved from his Washington, D.C., home onto a military installation amid security threats attributed to Tehran.

Bessent made a public appearance Friday, sitting nearby as President Donald Trump addressed reporters in the White House briefing room.

"Are you interviewing from a military base sewer right now, sweetie?" Iran's South African embassy posted on X alongside a screenshot of Bessent from an earlier television interview.

An Iranian official confirmed to Fox News Digital that the X account belongs to the embassy.

TRUMP'S TOP OFFICIALS RETREAT BEHIND MILITARY GATES AS EX-FBI DEPUTY POINTS TO WHAT'S FUELING THREATS

Bessent is the latest senior Trump administration official to relocate to a military base, joining a growing number of top officials living behind military gates as federal authorities confront security threats extending beyond the White House.

"Obviously, it's a high threat level for us to move," Bessent said while addressing the move during a Nov. 15 appearance on Fox Business' "Sunday Futures with Larry Kudlow."

A source familiar with the situation previously told Fox News Digital, "After The Wall Street Journal published an article featuring an online photo that allowed the location of the secretary’s Georgetown home to be geo-located, security concerns began to increase, which have now forced the secretary to relocate to a military base for his safety.

"The news media has an obligation to act responsibly amid growing threats against public officials."

BESSENT BLASTS NEWSPAPER EDITOR OVER 'RECKLESS JOURNALISM' AFTER IRAN THREATS FORCE MOVE TO MILITARY BASE

Threats against Bessent had reached "more than an advanced stage" amid reported Iranian assassination threats, a senior administration official told Fox News Digital when news broke of the decision to move the Treasury secretary on base. The official did not elaborate on the nature of the threats.

Attorney General Todd Blanche, Secretary of State Marco Rubio, Secretary of War Pete Hegseth, White House chief of staff Stephen Miller and other administration officials have moved to military installations or protected government housing.

Under Bessent, Treasury launched Operation Economic Outcast in August to disrupt Iran’s oil-smuggling, financial and cryptocurrency networks.

BESSENT WARNS IRAN'S OUTSIDE BACKERS TO 'STAY AWAY' AS TRUMP SEEKS TO 'ASPHYXIATE' TEHRAN'S ECONOMY

He said Treasury would "sever every economic lifeline" sustaining the Iranian regime and warned that entities facilitating money laundering for Tehran could be cut off from the U.S. dollar system.

Since then, Treasury has targeted Iran’s oil-smuggling shadow fleet, sanctioned eight Canada-based money services businesses it says helped Iranian entities move funds and moved to cut crypto exchange MEXC Global off from the U.S. financial system over alleged illicit transactions.

On Nov. 18, Treasury announced action against a gold-and-cash smuggling network it said was run by Hezbollah and Iran’s IRGC-Quds Force. Bessent said the U.S. would continue to "disrupt Iran’s attempts to exert influence in the region and fund its proxies."

item.title: Trump wags finger at 'really rude' reporter, tells her she belongs in the 'back row' during press exchange
item.description: Donald Trump wagged his finger at a reporter, calling her "really a rude person" and telling her she belonged in the "back row" at the White House.
item.content:encoded:
President Donald Trump rebuked a female reporter at the end of a White House news conference Friday, wagging his finger at her, calling her "really a rude person" and telling her she belonged in the "back row."

The exchange unfolded as Trump wrapped up a lengthy news conference following his return from an Asia trip, just after inviting White House Chief of Staff Stephen Miller to the podium and praising Miller's work on immigration and deregulation.

Before addressing the press corps, Trump defended Miller's temperament, noting that critics often view him as overly strict on immigration.

CHINA BLOCKS BLOOMBERG REPORTER FROM TRUMP-PUTIN-XI MEETING OVER QUESTION TO TRUMP

"He’s really a talent, and he’s got a big heart. A lot of people think he doesn’t. They think he’s hard on immigration, harder on this. He’s got a tremendous heart. In many ways. They think he’s got too big a heart. But we’ll talk about that," Trump said before breaking off to address the journalist.

"Who are you with. Who are you with?" Trump asked while waving his finger in her direction.

After the reporter replied, "Who are you?" Trump sharply criticized both her demeanor and her seating placement in the room.

JOE ROGAN SAYS PODCASTERS HAVE NO BUSINESS AT TRUMP PRESS CONFERENCES ALONGSIDE REAL JOURNALISTS

"And you’re really a rude person," Trump said.

When the reporter tried to speak again, beginning, "So if you’re talking about it," Trump cut her off and told her she should not be seated near the front of the press area.

"I’m not talking to you. I’m not telling you. You shouldn’t be in the front row. You should be in the back row," Trump said.

TRUMP AND DANA WHITE HONOR MARINE CORPS BAND WITH SIX-FIGURE CHECKS IN FIRST EVENT ON NEW HELIPAD

Trump then pivoted back to his closing remarks, inviting attendees to an afternoon ceremony and concert on the White House helipad with UFC CEO Dana White to honor and award money to U.S. military musicians.

"They’re unbelievably talented people, and we’re going to honor them in just a little while. And thank you for your fairness. Thank you for your questions. And Steve, thank you, J. D. Thank you. And Marco, thank you very much. Thank you everybody," Trump said as he concluded the appearance alongside Miller, Vice President JD Vance and Secretary of State Marco Rubio.

item.title: Firecracker Colts owner has America in a trance today, Sophie Cunningham buys protection & CBS's Jenny Dell!
item.description: Colts owner Carlie Irsay-Gordon went viral taking notes on the sidelines during a rough Thursday Night Football game, and the internet can't get enough.
item.content:encoded:
'Nightcaps' is a daily column that catches you up on the biggest sports, news and culture stories you may have missed while pretending to do work at your desk. It runs Monday-Friday on OutKick.com.

This is it, folks. The final Friday before Thanksgiving. The final Friday before Black Friday, if that's even a thing anymore. The final weekend before a holiday week — our first since Labor Day.

Been a while. We've worked our tails off the past few months to get back here. Sure, the stock market is collapsing all around us and our portfolios are cooked, but it's still a FRIDAY.

Cheer up, buttercup. We've got FOOTBALL tonight, tomorrow, Sunday and Monday. We've got Thanksgiving Eve. We've got Thanksgiving. We've got Black Friday. And then, we've got another weekend!

Who has it better than us right now? Nobody. Let's roll.

Welcome to a Friday Nightcaps — the one where Colts owner Carlie Irsay-Gordon put the internet in a trance during an otherwise horrific Thursday Night Football game.

Lordy, that was bad. It might've just been the worst TNF I've ever seen, and buddy, that is a LONG list.

What else? I've got Sophie Cunningham buying her friends some protection, USC football communications girl Katie Ryan checks in, and with the big day in six days, I'd like to get a pulse on everyone's best turkey recipes this year.

I've done the same one for six years now. Not saying I'm in the market to switch it up, but I'd like to see what else is out there.

OK, grab you some cajun seasoning, a bottle of Italian dressing, and a 12-pound bird, and settle in for a Friday 'Cap!

That's basically my recipe, by the way. It's simple, and it's never steered me wrong.

I inject the bird with Italian dressing. I then rub her down with a mixture of creole seasoning (the green bottle on every shelf in America), black pepper, cayenne pepper and garlic powder. I usually tone down the pepper and cayenne based on my audience. If you like it spicy, by all means, go for it.

SOPHIE CUNNINGHAM'S 4 AM HOTEL HALLWAY DANCE PARTY GOES VIRAL, INSTAGRAM LADIES WHO SERVED & #MACTION

But that's it. You mix those things together (1 cup creole, 1/4 cup black pepper, 2 TBSPs garlic power, 1/8 cup cayenne) however you'd like, and it'll create a sort of paste. Slather it all over the bird, stick her in the fridge overnight, and then fry her up the next day.

By all means, though, I'd love to hear what you all do. Again, I'm open to calling an audible this year if something sticks out.

Wow me! Zach.Dean@OutKick.com.

Now, let's get this Friday class started with the lunatic Colts owner who stands on the sidelines during every single game and takes notes about how truly horrible her team is.

I can't get enough of this woman:

What do we think Carlie Irsay-Gordon is writing down? Seriously. If you sat through that horrible game last night, what do YOU think she wrote down?

I can't get enough of Carlie just invading the sidelines for every single game and standing right behind the coach. How absolutely miserable must that be? Could you imagine your boss just standing behind your desk all day watching your every move?

I used to have a boss like that way back in the day.

Every time we saw him coming towards us, we'd let out an audible groan. We couldn't help it. He was too dumb to ever figure out we were groaning about him.

DANIEL JONES, JONATHAN TAYLOR REACT TO COLTS FIRE SALE AS THEY REMAIN PUT: 'YOU'RE NOT HAPPY TO SEE IT'

Those were the days. Simpler times.

OK, let's keep this class moving and check in with Sophie Cunningham, who is currently groaning at all the unprotected sex her friends have been having lately:

So, Sophie is going viral today for that above TikTok in which she vows to buy her friends condoms this holiday season because they're having too many kids, too fast.

Not sure how that's going to play with Sophie's base, but, to be fair, she also says it's great to have kids and we need more babies in the world. So, she plays both sides of the fence here pretty well.

It did get me thinking ... how old were you when you realized all your friends now had kids? One of my college buddies just had his first kid a few weeks ago, making him the third of our old college suit (shoutout to 1008!) to have kids. I was the first, by a mile. But I also got married before any of them because I'm from the south and that's what we do down here.

item.title: Somali community leaders bristle at broad blame even as youth gang violence surges from Minnesota to Maine
item.description: Ramsey County Sheriff Bob Fletcher says about 100 of 300 young alleged Somali gang members in the Twin Cities were arrested, but many cycle back into gang life.
item.content:encoded:
Somali community members in Minnesota pushed back Thursday against blaming the broader Somali American population as law enforcement officials warned of a surge in youth gang violence.

Members of the Somali community and law enforcement leaders met to discuss gang-related crimes in the Twin Cities, KSTP 5 Eyewitness News reported Thursday. 

Ramsey County Sheriff Bob Fletcher estimates there are about a dozen Somali gangs involving roughly 300 young people in the metro area out of an estimated 1,000 to 2,000 total gang members across the region.

Fletcher said many gang members who do get arrested ultimately continue participating in "the gang life."

CULTURE CLASH LAID BARE AS VIOLENT SOMALI GANGS GRIP SUBURBAN COMMUNITIES: ‘THESE KIDS ARE DIFFERENT’

"Well, many of them are [arrested]. I mean, we’ve arrested probably 100 of those 300," Fletcher told KSTP 5 Eyewitness News. "Many of them cycle out. Just because you arrest them doesn’t mean they’re not going to continue to participate in the gang life."

The Ramsey County Sheriff's Office did not respond to Fox News Digital's request for comment Friday.

However, some people at the community meeting said the Somali community in the Twin Cities metro area is being singled out unfairly.

Abdirizak Bihi, a Somali American social activist, said Thursday that "we cannot arrest our way" into fixing youth crime, KSTP 5 Eyewitness News reported.

"I’m concerned. I’m a father," Bihi said. "We cannot arrest our way into solving this problem for any youth.

"Of course, anyone who commits a crime, we have laws."

MINNESOTA HOMECOMING SHOOTING SUSPECT OUT ON BOND AFTER GUNFIRE SENDS FOOTBALL FANS FLEEING; 3 OTHERS ARRESTED

Minnesota Bureau of Criminal Apprehension Superintendent Drew Evans suggested that preventing gang violence can be "difficult to measure," CBS News reported Thursday.

"What a meeting like this does is it brings (the) community together in a way to really understand what the drivers of violence are to begin with," Evans said. "Prevention is always going to be difficult to measure. You're not going to be able to prove the negative if something didn't occur."

The tensions in the Twin Cities mirror similar struggles in other U.S. cities with large Somali American populations, where local officials and community leaders are also grappling with spikes in youth gun violence and debates over how to confront it.

In Lewiston, Maine, police reported 35 gun-related incidents this year, including 22 that involved juveniles, Fox News previously reported in October. The city houses a large population of Somali refugees and refugees from other African nations.

"I don’t feel safe. I fear for my life," Mohamed Muhumed, a Lewiston teenager, previously told Fox News Digital. "I saw someone get punched in the middle of the sidewalk over there. It’s crazy."

Maine Immigrant and Refugee Services Executive Director Rilwan Osman and his team unveiled a Voices Against Gun Violence program in June, which included daily workshops and community discussions throughout the month as part of a broader effort to address youth gun violence in the city, WGME reported June 1.

"We are asking people to pledge that they can talk about gun violence at home in their communities, at school, outside their school," Osman said, according to WGME.

The Minnesota BCA announced in an Oct. 19 news release that more than 40 law enforcement agencies agreed to "use an existing investigative model to coordinate efforts and strengthen collaboration in addressing gang and group violence." The plan also "employs county-based quick reaction teams for specialized and rapid uniformed patrol and investigative response when criminal activity occurs," according to the agency.

When reached for comment about its efforts to address gang-related crime in Minnesota, the BCA referred Fox News Digital to its Oct. 19 news release.

SOMALIS IN MINNESOTA UNLEASH FURY ON TRUMP AFTER FEDS RAID ILHAN OMAR'S DC HOME

Former state Trooper John Nagel told Fox News Digital in October that some Minnesota Democrats have their "heads in the sand" and hindered law enforcement from stopping Somali American gang-linked violence in the state before it escalated.

"They're being restrained by politicians, people that are trying soft on crime, people that are trying to send somebody other than a police officer to take care of issues, and it's not working," Nagel said at the time.

Police in Eden Prairie, Minnesota, previously said an Oct. 2 shooting outside Aerie Stadium at Eden Prairie High School's homecoming was connected to Somali gang activity.

About 84,000 Somali individuals live in the Minneapolis-St. Paul area, PBS News reported in December 2025.

SIGN UP TO GET THE POLITICS NEWSLETTER

Rep. Tom Emmer, R-Minn., sent a letter to U.S. Attorney Daniel Rosen July 23 flagging concerns about the "alarming rise" of Somali gang violence in the North Star State.

"I’ve said it before, and I’ll say it again. If you won’t assimilate, then get the hell out of here. First it was an estimated $9 billion in fraud. Now it’s out-of-control violence," Emmer said in a statement. "These Somali gangs have shot up high school graduations and assaulted players on opposing basketball teams with tire irons. It’s absolute madness, and something must be done."

In Columbus, Ohio, police announced the arrests, indictments or convictions of 21 BL-800 gang members in February 2024, WOSU 89.7 NPR News reported. 

Det. Eric Clouse said that the "BL" in the gang's name initially stood for "Bantu Life" or "Bantu Love" in reference to Somalia's Bantu ethnic community, according to the outlet.

Fox News' Paul Steinhauser contributed to this report.

item.title: Trump responds after Vance blames Iran war for midterm losses, VP says his job is to support president
item.description: President Donald Trump says he would launch the war against Iran again, as JD Vance blames midterm losses on voter anger over the conflict and oil prices.
item.content:encoded:
President Donald Trump said Friday that he would still have launched the military operation against Iran, pushing back against reports of friction with Vice President JD Vance after Vance attributed Republican midterm election losses to the ongoing conflict.

Speaking to reporters following his trip to Asia, Trump addressed questions about whether he was displeased with Vance’s post-election assessment that the conflict drove Democratic gains in the next Congress.

"I didn't say I was unhappy with it," Trump said alongside Vance and Secretary of State Marco Rubio. "I thought the statement was fine, except I would have had one other thing that if we're asked, I would have said that: ‘Would you do it again?’ Absolutely. The answer is yes, because we cannot allow Iran to have a nuclear weapon."

VANCE'S SCATHING IRAN WAR POSTMORTEM PUTS POTENTIAL 2028 GOP SHOWDOWN IN FOCUS: 'EVERYONE KNOWS WHY'

The remarks followed a series of posts on X by Vance a day after the midterm elections, in which Democrats won majorities in both the House and the Senate — along with the Texas governorship — blaming voter frustration over the conflict and elevated oil prices.

"The reason we lost is the war. The president himself said so last night," Vance wrote. "If you’d like to argue it was worth it, that losing the Senate for the next six years was worth it, then do so. Argue it was a worthwhile cost to pay. Agree or disagree, that’s at least honest. But everyone knows why we lost. And any honest conversation about where we go from here must start there."

VANCE COURTING DISGRUNTLED TRUMP VOTERS TO FORM ‘NEW RIGHT’ ALLIANCE AFTER REPUBLICAN BLOODBATH, SOURCES SAY

On Friday, Trump called Vance's assessment "accurate" and acknowledged that fuel costs rose amid the fighting, though he said the spike was milder than anticipated.

"The war drove up prices, fuel prices far less than I thought," Trump said. "I thought it would go up to $300 a barrel. You know, it's almost down to $80 a barrel right now."

FOX NEWS VOTER POLL: 2026 MIDTERM ELECTIONS USHER IN A BLUE WAVE AS DEMOCRATS WIN CONTROL OF CONGRESS

Despite the political fallout, Trump maintained that the military action was necessary to counter Tehran’s nuclear ambitions and to protect Israel and other Middle Eastern nations.

Vance affirmed that preventing Iran from obtaining a nuclear weapon justified the political cost, while emphasizing his alignment with Trump.

RUBIO DEFENDS TRUMP'S IRAN WAR AS NOT 'NECESSARILY POPULAR, BUT NECESSARY'

"What I've said is the goal of keeping Iran from getting a nuclear weapon is absolutely what we need to be doing," Vance said. "It's the biggest state sponsor of terrorism. If they had a nuclear weapon, they would use it as leverage or, God forbid, they would attack and kill thousands, hundreds of thousands, potentially, of innocent people."

"I think the president is the one who makes the decision, and the president has said he would do it again," Vance added. "My view is that my goal, and my job, is to support the president of the United States."

item.title: Why the under looks like the play in Kentucky vs Indiana as both teams bring solid defense
item.description: Kentucky Wildcats meet Indiana Hoosiers in a college basketball showdown, with the 4-1 Wildcats unranked and the 5-0 Hoosiers riding a tough schedule.
item.content:encoded:
Friday night is jam-packed with great games across all leagues and levels. We have the NBA Cup, NHL games, College Football and College Basketball all going tonight. Next week marks what I consider the true beginning of the College Basketball season. We get Thanksgiving tournaments, and then we start getting some of the conference games beginning shortly thereafter. We have had some great matchups recently, and now we have another with Kentucky vs. Indiana.

The Kentucky Wildcats come into the game with a 4-1 record, but they are unranked at the moment. Kentucky has struggled to find their footing in the years since John Calipari left the school. They still get some strong talent and good players, but they don't seem to find ways to make it work effectively enough. The team tends to get ranked somewhere in the mid-teens but never gets much higher. In fairness, the program started to struggle even before Coach Cal left.

KENTUCKY NEEDS BUZZER-BEATING THREE TO SURVIVE NORTHERN ARIZONA'S UPSET BID AT RUPP ARENA

In the past two seasons, the team has gone a combined 46-26. They played in the Sweet 16 two years ago, but they lost easily to Tennessee. Last year, they were bounced in the second round of the tournament. This season, they've beaten Manhattan to start the season, and then had a close-ish win over James Madison, winning by nine. Then, they lost to Kansas, one of the better teams in the country, and it wasn't just a loss; they were demolished, losing by 20. They barely beat Northern Arizona in their next game, but took some frustration out on Grambling.

Indiana hasn't been the picture of consistency themselves. At least not in a good way. They are 5-0 this season, which is a nice beginning. However, the Hoosiers have lost at least 12 games in each of the past 10 seasons. They've had sporadic moments when they were ranked, but they haven't been to the Sweet 16 since 2016. Perhaps this is the year the team can move up in the ranks and build off the positive start to the season. There is reason for hope, as they have some decent players on the squad.

SIGN UP FOR THE DAILY OUTKICK NEWSLETTER

To Indiana's credit, they've had a fairly tough schedule to start the season. They crushed Eastern Illinois and Bellarmine to start the year, and then faced Syracuse. That game happened on a neutral court, and they won by three points.

However, much like tonight's game, being on a neutral court is misleading because it was played in the Pacers' stadium. They beat Tennessee Tech, and then on Tuesday they took down Arkansas, the lone ranked team they've faced. That game was actually neutral because it was played in New York.

Kentucky is built around balance on the court. They have a strong guard, center, and forward. Milan Momcilovic is on this team after being at Iowa State for the past three seasons. That can make Kentucky difficult to guard, but it doesn't feel like they've found a way to cohesively organize this offense. The Hoosiers are a deep team. They have a strong backcourt, with six guys averaging 10 or more points per game. However, only Markus Burton is shooting well from deep. I do feel like Indiana will cover the short spread, but I prefer to take the under 154.5. Both teams are playing pretty solid defense. Additionally, this game will be played inside a football stadium, and teams tend to shoot poorly in those situations. Give me under 154.5.
